On Nov 6, 2028, at 11:03 AM, lukas.meyer@redwood.ai wrote:
>
> Proposed agenda:
> - Quick recap of Aurora's retention & PII constraints (5m)
> - Recommended export topologies...

Lukas — thanks, that agenda looks good. A couple of high-priority constraints from our side:
- No logs containing 3rd-party customer PII can be forwarded outside our VPC without tokenized redaction. We want to see redaction rules and where they run.
- We need TLS+MUTual auth for any HEC endpoint; cert rotation cadence must be documented.
- Sampling must preserve parent_id/trace_id for cross-service correlation but we will reject any open-text payloads (error messages) that include credit-card fragments or email addresses.

One more: we'll require a simple acceptance test that proves a sanitized trace/log pair was transmitted and can be mapped back to an internal request id (for audit). Can Redwood supply a test harness or runbook steps?

Thanks — Jared
Senior Security Engineer — AuroraData
From: lukas.meyer@redwood.ai <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@auroradata.com>, Sasha Miller <sasha.m@auroradata.com>

Subject: Re: Observability export patterns for our VPC private deployment

Jared / Sasha — great points, thank you. Short summary of decisions and next steps from today's call:

Decisions:
- Export topology: preferred pattern is a local forwarder (customer side) that pushes to a mutually authenticated Redwood private HEC endpoint inside Aurora's VPC. For on-prem where outbound is restricted, we document a TLS-based pull/forwarder bridge option (runbook section 3).
- Scrubbing: primary redaction must run at the collector boundary (customer-owned forwarder) using the scrub_rules_v1 policy. Redwood will publish a hardened ruleset (scrub_rules_v1.1) and a policy validator.
- Traces: sampling hooks will preserve trace_id/parent_id; error messages longer than 128 chars are truncated; any detected CC/email tokens are stripped.
- Acceptance test: Redwood will provide a minimal harness (curl + test payload) that demonstrates sanitized log + trace pair and a mapping key. Link below.

Action items:
- Lukas: produce runbook_obsv_onramp.md with step-by-step handoff + cert rotation section (ETA: 2028-11-10).
- Kimberly: finalize scrub_rules_v1.1 and push policy validator (ETA: 2028-11-12).
- Mina: provide the compliance checklist and a list of artifacts Aurora should preserve for audit (ETA: 2028-11-09).
- Aurora (Sasha/Jared): share final retention constraints and any additional schema that must be redacted (ETA: 2028-11-09).

Runbook / test harness: https://drive.redwood.internal/drive/folders/aurora-obsv-2028 (see runbook_obsv_onramp.md — attached in folder).

Attachments included in thread: runbook_obsv_onramp.md (markdown, 12KB), scrub_rules_v1.pdf, aurora_export_sample.jsonl

If that aligns, we'll spin up a short acceptance run with Aurora's staging forwarder next week.

Thanks,
Lukas
Integration Architect — Redwood Inference
